newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 14.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- NATWEST SUSPENDS FOUR MANAGERS

National Westminster Bank has suspended four more senior managers following substantial losses by its investment banking arm NatWest Markets. One manager in the division was suspended two weeks ago. The latest moves come as the bank revealed that the losses have now risen to 90 million stg. NatWest, which said it would write off 77 million stg against its first half profits to cover losses, is also to recoup part of the loss by cutting eight million stg from staff bonuses.
-- GEC-MARCONI SECURES TWO BILLION STG SUBMARINE DEAL

GEC-Marconi, the defence arm of GEC, is set to receive a two billion stg order from the Ministry of Defence for three Trafalgar-class nuclear submarines. The vessels will be built at GEC's VSEL shipyard in Barrow, which earlier this week won a separate 200-million-stg order from the MoD for two oil tankers for the Royal Navy. A final announcement on the submarine deal is expected shortly, and the news will secure jobs for around 2,500 VSEL workers.
-- ROW OVER TRAINING SUBSIDIES AT ACCOUNTS FIRMS

The Labour party has condemned plans by leading accountancy firms and training companies to use taxpayers' money to subsidize the training of accountants. Under the scheme, which has been approved by the government but strongly criticised within the profession, training fees could be cut by one third. The government's aim with the scheme was to allow more people, or people who would otherwise not be taken on, to get training. However, critics say the plan will simply subsidise training that large accountancy firms would have done anyway.
-- BRUSSELS LOSES BATTLE OVER CAR SPARE PARTS

Fierce lobbying by the car industry of ministers from EU member states has succeeded in denying the European Commission its aim of reducing the dominance of big vehicle makers in the European market for car spare parts. The ministers rejected a Commission proposal to allow independent part manufacturers to reproduce freely car spares such as bumpers, windscreens, door panels and lamps, on condition that the independents pay a 'fair and reasonable' royalty to the car manufacturers.
-- INDUSTRY HITS AT PROPOSAL TO RAISE FUEL TAXES

Industry across Europe has condemned European Commission proposals to raise the minimum tax rates on car and heating fuels and to extend them for the first time to natural gas and electricity. The proposals are aimed at ironing out distortions in the single market caused by different national tax regimes, and to encourage countries to shift taxation off labour and onto non-renewable sources. However, industry has claimed the plans, which are unlikely to become law, would erode competitiveness.
-- US GROUP BACKS WINDFALL LEVY

The chief executive of one of the US corporations that has bought into a UK regional electricity company has offered partial support for the Labour party's proposed windfall tax on the privatized utilities. James Rogers, chief executive of Cinergy Corp, which is co-owner of Midlands Electricity, said he was confident that Labour would apply the tax in a 'fair and reasonable' manner, and dismissed calls from other US companies to lobby Labour leader Tony Blair to withdraw the levy.
-- BP INCREASES BOARD'S PAY TO 13.1 MILLION STG

Annual reports published by oil company BP show the total renumeration paid to its board of directors has risen from 4.51 million stg to 13.1 million stg after the first share awards under the company's long-term performance scheme. Under the scheme, which is measured by the group's shareholder returns against seven rival oil companies, the directors will not be able to cash in the shares until 2001. The company said the awards were payable following its clear outperformance of the other major oil companies.
-- BT IN BID LINK WITH NTT

A joint bid by BT and Japan's NTT for Singapore's second national telecoms licence has prompted speculation that the two groups are considering stronger links. NTT, the world's largest telecoms company, is to be freed next year to compete in international markets. It has said it is seeking strategic overseas partners, but rejected overtures from BT to join Concert, its planned international alliance with MCI.
-- ENTERPRISE OIL ADVANCES 40 PERCENT

UK oil group Enterprise Oil has reported a 40 percent increase in net profit to 142.5 million stg. Announcing the results, which included a 33 percent rise in turnover to 1.01 billion stg, the company dampened speculation that it was planning an imminent takeover. Enterprise said it expects discoveries in the UK, Norway, Italy and the Gulf of Mexico would boost reserves, and increased its production forecasts to 320,000 barrels of oil a day by 1999.
-- VEBA ATTACKS BONN OVER TELECOMS

The chairman of German industrial group Veba, which is planning a telecoms joint venture with fellow industrial group RWE, has criticised the government in Bonn for failing to decide vital details of the liberalisation of the country's public telephone market due next January. Ulrich Hartmann attacked the failure to announce the line up of the country's proposed new telecoms regulatory authority. Veba and RWE are collaborating on o.tel.o, a DM7 billion ($4.1 billion) telecoms venture aimed at taking revenues of DM7 billion to DM9 billion by 2005.
